rounds.text: Sejal Glass Ltd demonstrates exceptional financial performance, driven by explosive top-line and bottom-line expansion, including a 5-year compounded sales growth of 109% and a TTM profit growth of 93% [E14, E19]. The company exhibits elite profitability and capital efficiency, boasting a median 3-year return on equity of 29% and a current ROE of 31.1%, comfortably outperforming the sector benchmark of 11.24% [E9, E23]. This underlying business strength is recognized by rules-based systems, generating a high-confidence BUY score of 95 out of 100 alongside a favorable sector tailwind in Capital Goods [E60, E68]. Furthermore, intrinsic valuation models indicate substantial mispricing, with a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 1359 providing a 36.1% margin of safety against the current market price of Rs 868, while the reverse DCF reveals that the market merely prices in an 11.8% growth rate against an 18.0% base case assumption [E40, E41, E42]. Operational cash generation remains robust, backed by a strong cash conversion of 1.76x for March 2026 where operating cash flow reached Rs 51 Cr [E29, E30]. Conceded: debt exceeds net worth with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.21x, free cash flow was negative at Rs -46 Cr in March 2026, and promoter holding decreased to 69.08% [E31, E32, E36].

Sejal Glass Ltd carries structural risks in its balance sheet and valuation that are masked by top-line growth. The company operates with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.21x, meaning its total debt exceeds its net worth, creating substantial leverage risk while borrowings increased to Rs 210 Cr [E32, E34]. This heavy debt burden is compounded by negative free cash flow of Rs -46 Cr in March 2026, alongside an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend over the last two years and two quarters respectively [E31, E27, E28]. Valuation multiples also outpace sector benchmarks, with a P/E of 25.96x against a sector benchmark of 22.02x, a P/B of 6.23x versus 2.4x, and an EV/EBITDA of 15.07x compared to 12.26x [E6, E7, E11]. Furthermore, promoters have reduced their holdings significantly from 78.96% in December 2023 to 69.08% in September 2026, accompanied by negative institutional money flow and a 0.00% dividend yield despite reported profits [E36, E39, E4, E57]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong historical sales growth, a high return on equity of 31.1%, and an operating cash flow of Rs 51 Cr in March 2026 that fully backs reported profits [E13, E16, E30].

Conceded: [E31] regarding free cash flow, [E36] on promoter reduction, and [E57] on the zero dividend yield. However, the bear's emphasis on leverage ignores that operating cash flow stands strong at Rs 51 Cr with complete cash-backed profit conversion of 1.76x for March 2026 [E30, E29]. While multiples trade above sector medians, they are fully justified by superior fundamentals, including a stellar ROE of 21.78% to 31.1% against a sector benchmark of 11.24%, and an ROA of 7.34% beating the 6.19% sector rate [E6, E7, E9, E8, E13]. Furthermore, the margin expansion to 17% in September 2026 alongside a 188.9% surge in capital-work-in-progress demonstrates that reinvested capital is actively driving growth rather than sitting idle [E26, E35]. Finally, domestic institutional holdings have actually increased by 4.39 percentage points since December 2023, showing strong institutional backing despite a negative short-term signal [E38, E39].

Conceded: [E30] and [E29] regarding operating cash flow and cash conversion. However, the bull's dismissal of leverage is entirely unjustified given that debt exceeds net worth with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.21x and borrowings have climbed to Rs 210 Cr [E32, E34], while free cash flow sits deeply negative at Rs -46 Cr [E31]. Furthermore, pointing to superior fundamentals does not erase the valuation premium where the P/B ratio reaches 6.23x against a sector benchmark of 2.4x and EV/EBITDA prints at 15.07x versus 12.26x [E7, E11]. The bull cites the 188.9% surge in capital-work-in-progress as productive reinvestment [E35], but this massive build-up phase merely highlights uncompleted projects carrying execution risks. Finally, while domestic institutional holdings rose over a multi-year period [E38], the current short-term institutional money flow reads negative with a holding drop [E39], and the historical record shows a catastrophic peak-to-trough drawdown of -100.0% alongside extreme annualized volatility of 7796.6% [E48, E49].

Conceded: [E32, E34] regarding debt exceeding net worth and rising borrowings, and [E31] concerning negative free cash flow. However, the bear's focus on valuation ratios ignores the powerful profitability metrics backing that price, including a 31.1% ROE and a 3-year median ROE of 29% [E13, E23], which completely justify a premium over the sector benchmark [E7, E11]. The massive 188.9% surge in capital-work-in-progress represents aggressive growth spend currently underway [E35], supported by robust operating cash flow of Rs 51 Cr and strong 1.76x cash conversion where profits are fully backed by cash [E29, E30]. While the bear highlights recent institutional outflow [E39], it ignores the broader picture that domestic institutional holdings have grown significantly to 4.39% from zero since December 2023 [E38]. Finally, citing historical drawdowns and volatility [E48, E49] is entirely disconnected from current technical reality, given that the stock trades above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a relative-strength rating of 100 [E45, E46].

Conceded: domestic institutional holdings grew to 4.39% from zero since December 2023 [E38]. While strong operating cash flow and cash conversion of 1.76x are noted [E29, E30], they are entirely consumed by aggressive capital spend while total debt expands [E34, E35]. Furthermore, the dismissive attitude toward institutional outflow [E39] and historical volatility metrics [E48, E49] overlooks the hard facts of a -100% worst peak-to-trough drawdown and an astronomical annualised volatility of 7796.6% [E48, E49]. Finally, justifying a rich P/B of 6.23x and EV/EBITDA of 15.07x over sector benchmarks purely on high past returns [E7, E11, E13, E23] ignores inconsistent operating margin trends [E27, E28] and ongoing negative institutional money flow [E39].
